title: Rachel and Leah (Genesis 29)
hookLine: Jacob works seven years for love and is tricked by his uncle

cards: Jacob arrives in his uncle Laban's country at a well, of course, because in Genesis the important meetings happen at wells. A shepherd girl comes with her father's flock. Her name is Rachel.
Jacob rolls the heavy stone off the well's mouth by himself, waters her sheep, kisses her, and bursts into tears. Love at first sight, at a well, in the middle of the day.
And the man who tricked his blind father is about to meet someone even better at tricks than he is.

teach.b: First, the bargain. Laban has two daughters: Leah, the elder, whose eyes the text calls weak or tender, and Rachel, the younger, beautiful. Jacob offers seven years of work for Rachel.
Then one of the loveliest lines in Genesis, in the Douay-Rheims: "So Jacob served seven years for Rachel: and they seemed but a few days, because of the greatness of his love." Second, the trick.
On the wedding night, Laban sends in Leah, veiled, in the dark. In the morning, Jacob finds Leah. Why hast thou deceived me?

And Laban answers that in their country, the younger isn't given before the firstborn. The man who disguised himself as the firstborn has been fooled by a firstborn in disguise. Genesis doesn't point it out.
It doesn't need to. Jacob works seven more years for Rachel. Third, the one nobody chose.
Leah is married to a man who loves her sister, and here the text turns its eye to her: the Lord, seeing that Leah was despised, opened her womb. She names her sons as if she's talking to God.
Reuben: the Lord saw my affliction. Simeon: the Lord heard. Levi: now my husband will be joined to me.
Then the fourth, Judah, and something shifts. This time I will praise the Lord. No mention of the husband.

teach.h: LEVI THE PRIESTS, JUDAH THE KINGS.
teach.b: Levi becomes the tribe of priests.

teach.h: THIS TIME I WILL PRAISE THE LORD.
teach.b: Judah becomes the line of King David, and, Matthew's Gospel says, of Jesus. The unchosen wife is the mother of both.

how: Catholics remember Rachel and Leah among the mothers of Israel; the Church's traditional wedding blessing once asked that the bride be loving like Rachel, and Leah's son Judah is named in Jesus's genealogy read at Christmas.

o: the son of Jacob from whom the kings came
Leah's firstborn: the Lord saw my affliction
Rachel's firstborn, born after long waiting

games.q: what's inside the sisters' story — tap the pairs.
p: this time I will praise the Lord

s: Jacob works seven years in total for Rachel
he works seven, is tricked into marrying Leah, and works seven more.
Leah is the mother of both Levi and Judah
the tribe of priests and the line of David, and in Matthew, of Jesus.
Genesis points out that Jacob the trickster has been tricked
it never says so. it lets the echo speak: the younger and the firstborn, in disguise again.

games.q: you're Leah, married to a man who loves your sister. you've just had your fourth son. what do you name him, and why?
o: a name asking your husband to love you at last.
Judah: this time I will praise the Lord.
a name honoring your sister Rachel.
games.why: her first three names reach for her husband. with Judah she says, this time I will praise the Lord, and that son becomes the line of kings.

practice: Think of someone living in second place right now: the sibling who's always compared, the friend invited last, the one in a family where someone else gets the warmth.
Hold them in mind, and remember the order of Leah's names: three sons named for the love she hoped her husband would give, a fourth named for praise.
If you pray, ask that this person find a place where love doesn't have to be earned.

wordCard.voice: Reuben, Leah's firstborn, whose name means the Lord saw: hers was the first cry from the wife nobody chose. Today's word.

orig.note: Hebrew: Reuben, see, a son. Leah hears in it that the Lord saw her affliction.

carryVoice: Your line: leah was seen. God's eye went to the one left out. That's the week.
